turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is this... this constant restless feeling I’ve been having. It’s like I’m wound way too tight all the time and I just can’t fully settle down. Even when I’m supposed to be calmly sitting through a planning meeting for work—I'm a wholesale buyer, so we have these incredibly long meetings about next season's inventory. We're looking at a lot of really beautiful jewel tones for the fall line, actually. 

Which reminds me, I even tried taking up painting recently to see if it would help me unwind. Just watercolors, you know? I love how the pigments bleed into the paper, it's supposed to be very therapeutic. My sister is the real artist in the family, she does these massive oil canvases, but I don't have the patience to wait for oil paint to dry. But anyway, even when I'm sitting there painting, or when I'm trying to do yoga—I joined that new studio downtown with the gorgeous bamboo floors?—I just... I can't relax. I can't settle. I'm just always wound up instead of actually relaxing into it.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly describes having a 'constant restless feeling' and an inability to fully settle down.
symptom_reasoning.S013: The patient reports being unable to relax or settle even when trying to engage in calming leisure activities like painting or yoga.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient describes feeling 'wound way too tight all the time' and being unable to relax, indicating physical tension and feeling keyed up.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had sudden, unexpected panic attacks?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really had anything like that. No sudden panic or anything. Just that constant restless feeling, you know? Like my motor is always running. My husband says I'm like a hummingbird. We actually have this hummingbird feeder out on our back deck—he got it for me for my birthday last year because I love watching them. They're so fast, it's incredible. We had to try three different types of nectar before we found one they actually liked, but now they come around all the time. The ruby-throated ones are my favorite, they're just so vibrant. But yeah, no panic attacks, I don't think. Just... always on the go.

turns.doctor_question: Did this restlessness start after a specific stressful event or life change?
turns.patient_response:
Not really, no. I can't think of any big stressful event or... or major life change that set it off. I mean, people kept asking me if turning 50 last year was stressful, but it honestly wasn't! My husband actually threw me this amazing surprise party at that little Italian place over on 4th street—Giovanni's? Have you been there? Oh, you really have to go, their garlic knots are just incredible. They bake them fresh every hour, you can literally smell them from down the block. 

My daughter even flew in from college for the party, which was the real surprise because she was right in the middle of midterms. She's studying marine biology out in California. It's so fascinating, but she has to take so much calculus for it. I was never good at math, which is kind of funny since I deal with wholesale budgets all day, but thank goodness for Excel spreadsheets, right? The formulas just do it all for you. But... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, stress. Yeah, no, nothing like that. I've just kind of always been this way, I think.

turns.doctor_question: Would you say the worrying or restlessness is hard for you to control?
turns.patient_response:
Worrying? No, I wouldn't say I worry. I'm not really an anxious person at all. My co-worker Brenda, now she's a worrier. She's always stressing out about the shipping delays from our overseas suppliers. Which, to be fair, the logistics have been an absolute nightmare lately. We had this whole shipment of cashmere blend sweaters stuck at the port for three weeks. And cashmere is so delicate, you know? You have to be so careful with how it's stored or moths will just ruin it in a heartbeat. I actually use these little cedar blocks in my own closets at home, they smell wonderful and they're completely natural. I get them from this lovely little artisan market on Sundays, the guy who carves them makes these beautiful little birdhouses too... 

But, um, wait, what did you ask? Oh, if it's hard to control. I don't know, I haven't really noticed trying to control the restless feeling, to be honest. I don't really try to stop it, it's just kind of how my engine runs.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things most days?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. Like I said, I'm not much of a worrier. I just don't have that kind of brain that gets stuck on bad things that might happen. My brain just sort of... bounces around to whatever's happening right now. Like yesterday, I was supposed to be finalizing our spring catalog orders, but I saw this pop-up ad for a gardening class at the community center, and before I knew it, I was researching heirloom tomato varieties for an hour. Did you know there's a tomato called the Cherokee Purple? It's supposed to be incredible for slicing. I love a good BLT in the summer. You have to use thick-cut bacon, though, the thin stuff just gets lost. My husband makes his own sourdough bread for them, he got really into baking during the pandemic and just never stopped. His starter is named 'Dough-lores' and he feeds it every single morning. It's practically a pet at this point. 

Anyway, what was the question? Worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really sit around worrying about things.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often have trouble concentrating or staying focused?
turns.patient_response:
Trouble concentrating? Oh, definitely. Like, especially over the past couple of years, it's gotten so frustrating. I'll be looking at a vendor spreadsheet, and I swear I've checked it so carefully. I'll go row by row, making sure everything lines up. But then our planning coordinator—her name is Sarah, she's an absolute lifesaver, honestly, she used to work in logistics for this huge international shipping company, so she catches everything. She actually speaks three languages, which is so impressive. I tried learning French on one of those apps once, but I could never remember to do my streak. The little green owl got so passive-aggressive! It would send me these notifications like, "These reminders don't seem to be working, we'll stop sending them." It actually made me feel guilty, if you can believe that. Guilted by an app! 

But anyway, Sarah will look at my spreadsheet and point out that I transposed a SKU, or completely missed a freight surcharge, or carried the wrong quantity over into the actual purchase order. And I'll look at it and think, how did I even do that? I was staring right at it! It's like my eyes just slide right off the numbers sometimes.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have similar trouble paying attention or staying organized when you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
When I was a kid? Oh, gosh, yeah. I remember in elementary school, my parents were constantly getting notes sent home from my teachers. I just could not stay put—I kept popping out of my seat, and I was always talking over my classmates. 

Actually, my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, used to write those notes on this specific pink stationery that smelled strongly of roses. It was so distinct, I can literally still smell it if I think about it. She was obsessed with roses, she even had this massive garden at her house. We actually did a class field trip there once, and I remember it poured rain the entire time, so we all had to wear these cheap plastic ponchos. Mine got caught on a thorn bush and ripped right down the side. I was so upset because I had this matching umbrella with little ducks on the handle. I was obsessed with ducks when I was little. My dad and I used to go to the local pond and feed them bread every Sunday, which I know now is actually terrible for their digestion, you're supposed to give them frozen peas or oats or something... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, Mrs. Gable's notes! But yeah, the notes were always about how I couldn't wait my turn. I'd always be rushing to answer before she even finished asking the question. So, yes, I definitely had trouble with that kind of stuff back then, too.
